chunks: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me:

Beware of taking each other for judgement to the people of injustice. But look for a man from among you who knows something of our rulings, then make him the arbiter between you — for I have indeed appointed him as a judge — so bring your disputes to him.

key_terms.أَهْلُ الْجَوْرِ: People of injustice/tyranny — refers to unjust rulers, judges, and their courts who do not govern by divine law
key_terms.قَاضِياً: Judge (qadi) — a qualified jurist authorized to settle disputes; the Imam's delegation of this role is significant for the doctrine of wilayat al-faqih
key_terms.قَضَائِنَا: Our rulings/judgements — the legal decisions and jurisprudence of the Imams (AS) transmitted through the Shia tradition

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about referring disputes to unjust judges?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) issues a strict prohibition against seeking judgement from unjust rulers and their courts, instead instructing the Shia community to appoint qualified jurists from within their own community. This narration is one of the foundational texts for the Shia doctrine of wilayat al-faqih (guardianship of the jurist), establishing that an Imam-appointed jurist has legitimate judicial authority during the Imam's absence. The original audience — Shia living under Abbasid rule — would have understood this as a practical safeguard: avoiding legitimization of unjust authority while ensuring community disputes are resolved by someone knowledgeable in Imami fiqh.
